description_md:
## Problem

Retail shops run sales, stock, purchasing, and finance as separate habits, and the stock count drifts away from the record. Price changes and purchase costs are hard to trace later, so cost of goods sold and inventory value come out wrong, and the owner has no single report to check the business against.

## Role & constraints

Solo full-stack work from October to November 2026, as a personal project. The code is public. The backend, the Vue frontend, and the PostgreSQL schema are mine.

## Approach

One web application keeps sales, products, inventory, suppliers, and purchasing together. It generates EAN-13 barcodes and prints product labels, records price history with scheduling and bulk updates, and runs stock opname through a physical count, an approval step, and a stock adjustment. Inventory value and cost of goods sold use a moving weighted average cost, which also feeds the gross-profit and margin reports. JWT authentication and role-based access keep ADMIN, OWNER, and CASHIER inside their own job.

## Result

The build covers 18 business features across 15 API route groups. Stock updates itself from sales, purchase receipts, returns, and adjustments, and an audit log records who changed what.

## Lessons

Keeping sales, purchases, returns, and stock adjustments consistent took the most work, because one action changes stock that the others read. Stock opname needed its own care: two people can count at the same time, so the approval step has to reject a second approval and keep the counter and the approver apart.
summary: Full-stack retail POS that ties sales, stock, purchasing, and finance together, with moving-average cost and a stock opname approval flow.
title: Retail Point of Sale (POS) System

description_md:
## Problem

Small restaurants and cafes run the till, the kitchen, and the stock on separate habits. The kitchen hears about an order when someone walks over with a paper slip, ingredient stock is guessed at the end of the day, and the numbers are written up by hand. When the owner asks what sold and what it cost, nothing lines up.

## Role & constraints

Solo full-stack work in November 2026, as a personal project. The code is public. The backend, frontend, database, and deployment are mine.

## Approach

A Go backend serves a REST API and a server-sent events stream, with a React frontend for the cashier, the kitchen display, and the admin pages, on PostgreSQL 16. Confirming an order cuts ingredient stock, writes the kitchen order, and sets the table to occupied in one database transaction, so a half-finished order cannot leave stock wrong. The kitchen screen updates over SSE per outlet. Every request that spends money or stock carries an idempotency key, so a retry never charges twice. Permissions are checked in the backend and denied by default.

## Result

The whole system runs on one VPS behind Nginx, with scheduled encrypted backups and an append-only audit log.

## Lessons

Order confirmation carries the most risk, so it sits in a single transaction that locks stock rows in a fixed order. I kept the backend as a modular monolith instead of separate services, because the extra moving parts would not pay off on one small server.
summary: Restaurant and cafe POS for small businesses: cashier, real-time kitchen display, tables, recipes, ingredient stock, shifts, and reports.
title: Food and Beverage POS (Restaurant & Cafe)

description_md:
## Problem

The previous version of the app was hard to use and its flow was confusing. It had no way to request an extra FAT pole, no AI to verify that a sales visit really happened, and no validation of customer identity, so the reported data could not be trusted.

## Role & constraints

Solo full-stack work from March to August 2026, as my final-year thesis. The code is private. I owned the backend, the Flutter app, the PostgreSQL schema, and the computer-vision model at the same time.

## Approach

I added OTP-based customer validation and a computer-vision module built on YOLO26 and PaddleOCR that detects and reads visit evidence, so a visit is confirmed by the system instead of by the salesperson's word. I simplified the business flow, added a request path for extra FAT poles, and rebuilt the interface in Flutter. FastAPI serves the API, PostgreSQL stores the data, and Redis handles caching for the reads that repeat most.

## Result

Visits are verified automatically and customers are confirmed with OTP, which removes the manual spot-checks. The hardest part was carrying backend, frontend, and the AI model in one project.
summary: Computer-vision and FastAPI system that validates FTTH sales data, verifies sales visits, and confirms customers by OTP.
title: Computer Vision for FTTH Sales Data Validation

description_md:
## Problem

Material records from raw material to finished goods were split across tools, so the position of a batch was hard to trace and some movements went unrecorded. Customs documents had to match the Bea Cukai format, where a manual check is easy to get wrong. Delivery notes were issued by hand, container and fleet positions could not be followed, and production data never reached finance, so costing was slow.

## Role & constraints

Full-stack work in a team of three, from January to April 2026, on a freelance engagement. The code is private.

## Approach

One platform ties production, inventory, distribution, and finance together. Every material movement is recorded, so origin and position can be traced at any time. The Customs API integration validates and reshapes the input data before it leaves the system, which keeps the documents defensible. Delivery notes are issued automatically and connect to a field-staff mobile app that tracks containers and the fleet in real time. Production and logistics data sync into a finance module for costing and period recaps.

## Result

Every stage of manufacturing is traceable, customs input is validated against the required format, and finance figures come from the same data instead of a manual retype.

## Lessons

Connecting to the Bea Cukai API and matching its exact data format was the real work: warehouse data has to pass validation before it is sent, or the customs document is not valid.
summary: Mini-ERP and logistics platform tracing manufacturing from raw material to warehouse, with a Customs API and finance module.
title: Integrated Mini-ERP and Logistics Management System

description_md:
## Problem

Field sales often missed their targets with no visibility, and some reported visits to locations they never visited. Managers had no way to check a claim.

## Role & constraints

Backend developer in a team of four, from August to December 2025, during my internship at PT Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison. The code is private.

## Approach

Sales log their visits in the app and the system verifies each one with AI detection, so a visit is an event the system confirms rather than a line the salesperson types. The backend exposes the visit and reporting endpoints and stores them in PostgreSQL.

## Result

Visit reports are no longer manual and are more accurate because they are verified by detection, which cuts false reporting. Used by 100 to 500 users across the sales team.
summary: Field-sales activity monitoring with AI-based visit verification to cut false reporting.
title: DSE AI — Field Sales Activity Monitoring

description_md:
## Problem

Sales did not know or forgot when and where to visit, managers could not follow activity in real time, and the daily report was still written by hand.

## Role & constraints

Backend developer in a team of seven, from August to December 2025, during my internship. The code is private.

## Approach

The system schedules visits on a Google Map, groups working areas by village, and supports tandem routes where two salespeople visit together. A daily-report dashboard shows each area's performance to managers, so the report is generated from recorded activity instead of a manual recap.

## Result

Daily reports are automatic, sales visits are easier to plan, and managers can follow area performance without asking for numbers. Used by 200 to 500 users across the sales team.
summary: Sales visit scheduling on Google Maps with a daily-report dashboard for managers.
title: Elang HUB — Sales Visit Scheduling and Reporting

description_md:
## Problem

Managers wanted an assistant that could answer questions about the daily report, and the report itself had to reach them every afternoon on WhatsApp, by hand.

## Role & constraints

Solo backend and automation work from August to December 2025, on a freelance engagement. The code is private.

## Approach

I automated the afternoon report push to WhatsApp and built a question-answering chatbot over the same report data. The chatbot is limited to a fixed list of phone numbers, and the prompt is tuned so the model understands the manager's context. Data is queried from PostgreSQL and the flows run on n8n, with KNIME in the analysis step.

## Result

Managers can see each area's performance quickly instead of waiting for a manual recap. Used by managers for two to three months.

## Lessons

Meta's rules do not allow a bot to message anyone at will, so the audience had to be explicit and opt-in.
summary: WhatsApp and Telegram daily-report automation and a chatbot that answers managers' performance questions.
title: Chatbot & Daily-Report Automation (WhatsApp/Telegram)

description_md:
## Problem

Predicting drinking-water quality in Indonesia against the Ministry of Health (Kemenkes RI) indicators was not available automatically, and the dataset was far too large to process by hand.

## Role & constraints

Data-science work in a team of two, from June to July 2025, as a course project. The code is private.

## Approach

I built an end-to-end PySpark pipeline over more than 1.2 million rows: cleaning, handling anomalous values, imputing nulls, and pivoting the features into a model-ready shape. A logistic-regression classifier in Spark MLlib predicts whether a water sample is safe to drink, evaluated with accuracy and AUC.

## Result

Accuracy of 88.62 percent and an AUC of 0.86, with the whole pipeline reproducible instead of a one-off notebook.

## Lessons

Cleaning data at this scale, across many features, is where most of the work and most of the risk lives.
summary: PySpark pipeline over 1.2M+ rows predicting drinking-water safety against Indonesian health-ministry standards.
title: Big Data Predictive Analysis of Drinking-Water Quality

description_md:
## Problem

Campus letters were still written in Microsoft Word with a fixed template, and signatures were still processed on paper.

## Role & constraints

Backend developer in a team of eight, from June 2024 to January 2025, as a course project. The code is public.

## Approach

The system lets a user create an official letter from a template at any time, administrators across departments track the process, and approval happens online so departments can reach the central admin without a phone call.

## Result

Letter creation dropped from 10 minutes to 2 minutes, and a letter can be reached from anywhere instead of only from the office.

## Lessons

Collecting the right templates from each department was harder than the code, and the paper signature that is scanned afterwards still has to fit into the flow.
summary: Campus letter system with template-based drafting, admin monitoring, and online approval.
title: SIRATA — Integrated Campus Letter System

description_md:
## Problem

Event organisers struggled to promote their events and sell tickets, and users had no single place to find an event and buy a ticket.

## Role & constraints

Full-stack work in a team of four, from July to August 2024, built for a competition. The code is public.

## Approach

Organisers register an event and sell tickets; users search, read the details, price, and how to buy, and then purchase. I built the backend and the event pages.

## Result

Organisers can publish and sell in one place, and users have one place to find an event and buy a ticket.

## Lessons

Studying how ticketing systems handle capacity and payment first saved rework later.
summary: Event and ticketing platform where organisers publish events and users find and buy tickets.
title: Campevent — Event and Ticketing Platform
